Internal helper: an expression given as the data that cannot be evaluated

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_expr_data_stop.Rd

The (S391) expression-typo item (Session 392): with d holding Score, Group and Age and dd a typo for it, jt(Score ~ Group, dd[dd$Age > 40, ]) printed R's own "object 'dd' not found", with no prefix – ruling R36 reads a NAME, and the data here is an expression – and the data-first functions read the expression as a variable: jfreq(dd[dd$Age > 40, ], Group) said it "needs a data frame" and offered jfreq(MyData, dd[dd$Age > 40, ]), Group dropped, and under a juse() default said it "was not found in the d data frame". When the expression a call gives as its data stops, the reason is said in the house voice, the first that applies:

  1. a column its data frame lacks – after $, in a literal [[ ]], or a name in subset()'s condition or select that is neither a variable of that frame nor an object (.jst_expr_missing_columns()): .jst_check_vars()'s sentence, "Agee was not found in the d data frame." / "Check the spelling.";

  2. a name that is no object and no variable of any data frame, R's message naming one of them (.jst_quoted_in()): "'dd' not found.", several named together (ruling R25), with tail after it when the caller has a line of its own to give. When it is one name, ruling R36's offer is tried first (.jst_expr_misspelled_offer());

  3. any other reason, by relay: "always" gives " could not be evaluated." / "R reported:" and R's message; "unless_variable" gives it unless R's message names a variable of a data frame – jsubset(Age > 40) with no frame named, an expression of variables that needs a data frame, which the caller says – and "never" leaves every other reason to the caller.

Usage

.jst_expr_data_stop(
  data_sub,
  err,
  fn,
  envir,
  cl = NULL,
  vars = NULL,
  offer = TRUE,
  relay = c("always", "unless_variable", "never"),
  tail = NULL,
  vector_ok = FALSE
)

Arguments

data_sub

The expression as typed.

err

The condition the evaluation raised, or R's message.

fn

Character(1). The user-facing function's name.

envir

The caller's environment.

cl

The call as typed, for the offered line; NULL for none.

vars

Character. The variables the call names besides the data; NULL reads them from cl, its unnamed arguments.

offer

Logical. FALSE for a function that refuses an expression as the data (jsubset(), jcomplete() and the registration verbs), whose offered line would stop there.

relay

"always", "unless_variable" or "never".

tail

Character or NULL. Lines after "'dd' not found." when no line is offered.

vector_ok

Logical. TRUE for jdesc(), jfreq() and jscreen(), which take a single column: the offered expression may give one (jfreq(d$Age) for jfreq(dd$Age)).

Value

Invisible NULL when the caller is to go on; otherwise stops.
